evidence.title: Makapansgat Limeworks (Limpopo, South Africa): Australopithecus africanus
evidence.dateBasis: Paleomagnetic polarity stratigraphy, U-Pb flowstone constraints, and biochronological correlations across Member 3–4 breccias.
evidence.summary: Rich South African dolomite cave breccia preserving Australopithecus africanus craniodental fossils and the famous natural ironstone 'Makapansgat pebble' carried in from kilometers away.
evidence.limits: Complex reworked karst infilling yields broader age brackets than single tuff horizons.

evidence.title: Swartkrans Cave Members 1–3 (Gauteng, South Africa): Paranthropus, early Homo & burned bone
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic 26Al/10Be burial (~2.2–1.8 Ma Member 1), U-Pb speleothems, and ESR tooth enamel dating.
evidence.summary: Co-occurrence of ~100 Paranthropus robustus individuals alongside early Homo/Homo erectus (SK 847, SK 15), shaped bone digging tools, and Member 3 (~1.0 Ma) intentionally burned animal bones.
evidence.limits: Taxonomic assignment of fragmented mandibles (SK 15) and exact fire control vs. wildfire wash-in remain active debates.

evidence.title: Kromdraai B (Gauteng, South Africa): Paranthropus robustus type site & infant crania
evidence.dateBasis: U-Pb speleothem and faunal correlation in Cradle of Humankind dolomitic breccias.
evidence.summary: Type locality where Robert Broom identified Paranthropus robustus (TM 1517) in 1938; recent excavations recovered juvenile KW 9600/KW 10840 craniofacial blocks revealing distinct Early Pleistocene ontogeny.
evidence.limits: Karst breccia blocks mix fine decalcified seams with eroded talus fills.

evidence.title: Omo Shungura Formation (Lower Omo Valley, Ethiopia): 2.8–1.4 Ma Paranthropus & early Homo
evidence.dateBasis: Ar-Ar dated volcanic tuffs (Tuffs C through K/L) sandwiching continuous alluvial Member sequences.
evidence.summary: Longest continuously tuff-calibrated Pliocene–Early Pleistocene sequence in eastern Africa yielding >200 hominin fossils (Paranthropus aethiopicus/boisei and early Homo) alongside Member F Oldowan quartz flake assemblages (~2.3 Ma).
evidence.limits: Isolated teeth predominate over complete crania, limiting intra-member morphological sampling.

evidence.title: Salé & Sidi Abderrahmane (Morocco): Middle Pleistocene NW African Homo
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, OSL, and marine-terrace biostratigraphy on Moroccan Atlantic calcarenite dunes.
evidence.summary: Landmark Northwest African Middle Pleistocene calvaria (Salé) and Grotte des Littorines mandibles alongside Thomas Quarry Acheulean cleavers—illustrating North African Maghreb hominin diversity prior to Jebel Irhoud.
evidence.limits: Older quarry salvage lacks single-tuff precision; revised 2026 Morocco studies anchor deeper Maghreb ancestry.

evidence.title: Lake Ndutu & Lake Eyasi (Northern Tanzania): Transitional Middle–Late Pleistocene crania
evidence.dateBasis: U-series and tephra correlation with Olduvai Masek/Ndutu Beds and Eyasi lakeshore sandstone.
evidence.summary: Mosaic East African crania blending thick archaic supraorbital/occipital traits with expanded braincases (~1,100–1,250 cc), illustrating mosaic African Homo sapiens origins rather than a single linear transformation.
evidence.limits: Historical surface finds at Eyasi yield broad minimum/maximum U-series age ranges.

evidence.title: Singa (Blue Nile, Sudan): Early Late Pleistocene Homo sapiens calvaria
evidence.dateBasis: Direct ESR and U-series dating on matrix caliche and associated equids from Blue Nile bank.
evidence.summary: Nearly complete Nile-basin Middle Stone Age human cranium showing globular parietal expansion alongside labyrinthine bony pathology, linking NE African Nile corridors to early sapiens diversification.
evidence.limits: Single calvaria recovered in 1924 limestone block; ear-bone pathology slightly distorts vault contours.

evidence.title: Ngaloba (Laetoli LH 18, Northern Tanzania): Transitional MSA Homo sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: Direct U-series and amino-acid racemization on ostrich eggshell in Ngaloba Beds above Olduvai tuff horizons.
evidence.summary: Well-preserved East African MSA cranium uniting modern facial proportions and slender brow geometry with slightly archaic long vault proportions, exemplifying multiregional Pan-African sapiens evolution.
evidence.limits: Original ~120 ka bracket rests partly on correlated lake-bed eggshell and mammalian fauna.

evidence.title: Eliye Springs (KNM-ES 11693, West Turkana, Kenya): Late Middle Pleistocene mosaic cranium
evidence.dateBasis: Biochronology and morphological stage correlation along eroded southwestern Lake Turkana beach deposits.
evidence.summary: Sub-complete mineralized Turkana cranium showing thick vault bone and broad face combined with rounded occipital contours—mirroring Florisbad and Jebel Irhoud transitional African diversity.
evidence.limits: Eroded surface beach find lacking primary volcanic ash seal prevents narrow radiometric precision.

evidence.title: Bir el Ater / Oued Djebbana (Tebessa, Algeria): Aterian Tanged Point Type Site
evidence.dateBasis: TL, OSL, and infinite radiocarbon ages (>35 ka) tied to regional Aterian Nassarius shell-bead horizons.
evidence.summary: Type station for the North African Aterian complex—distinctive tanged Levallois points designed for hafted spears/darts paired across nearby sites with Nassarius perforated marine-shell beads.
evidence.limits: Original 1920s–1950s alluvial gravel cuts lack high-resolution single-grain OSL re-excavation.

evidence.title: Ysterfontein 1 (Western Cape, South Africa): MIS 5c–5a Coastal Shell Midden
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & U-series ages across stratified calcrete-sealed coastal limpet and mussel middens.
evidence.summary: Intact Late Pleistocene West Coast MSA shoreline camp showing systematic limpet harvesting, red ochre crayons, silcrete/calcrete bladelet reduction, and coastal marine adaptation ~100 ka.
evidence.limits: Calcrete deflation limits preservation to a shallow coastal overhang.

evidence.title: Enkapune Ya Muto (Twilight Cave, Central Rift, Kenya): 46–40 ka MSA–LSA Bead Transition
evidence.dateBasis: Obsidian hydration, amino-acid racemization & AMS radiocarbon on ostrich eggshell beads in Rift Valley ash-cave layers.
evidence.summary: Landmark East African shelter preserving some of the world's oldest backed microlithic obsidian blades and finished ostrich-eggshell beads right across the Middle-to-Later Stone Age transition.
evidence.limits: Lower Sakutiek strata sit near the technical radiocarbon saturation frontier.

evidence.title: Hofmeyr Cranium (Eastern Cape, South Africa): 36 ka Sub-Saharan Homo sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: Direct OSL + U-series dating of carbonate endocast sediment inside the mineralized cranium (36.2 ± 3.3 ka).
evidence.summary: Rare Late Pleistocene sub-Saharan human skull (~36 ka) whose geometric morphometrics resemble European Upper Paleolithic crania more closely than recent Khoesan/Bantu series—supporting a shared ~40–60 ka pan-Eurasian/East African ancestor.
evidence.limits: Collagen completely leached so ancient nuclear DNA failed; age rests on endocast matrix OSL.

evidence.title: Shum Laka Basal Rockshelter (Cameroon Grassfields): >32 ka Humid Highland Foraging
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dating basal weathered quartz flake-tool assemblages beneath later Holocene Bantu-threshold burials.
evidence.summary: Continuous highland shelter demonstrating late Pleistocene quartz bladelet-and-flake foraging in Central-West Africa well before ~8,000–3,000 BP ancient-DNA burial phases.
evidence.limits: Acidity removed Pleistocene bone and pollen prior to Holocene ash-heap accumulation.

evidence.title: Apollo 11 Cave (ǂGoachanas, SW Namibia): ~30 ka Painted Portable Slabs
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS and OSL stratigraphic bracket on seven broken painted quartzite plaques in Layer E.
evidence.summary: Africa's oldest dated figurative portable paintings—charcoal and ochre depictions of rhinoceros/feline-bodied therianthropes buried inside Middle-to-Later Stone Age cave sediments.
evidence.limits: Original ~27–30 ka radiocarbon dates carry ±2 ka uncertainties around the Late Pleistocene boundary.

evidence.title: Korolevo I (Transcarpathia, Western Ukraine): 1.42 Ma Earliest Europe Gate
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic nuclide (26Al/10Be) P-burial and isochron dating by Garba et al. (2024) on lower andesite pebble-core Horizon VII.
evidence.summary: Oldest securely dated hominin stone-tool presence anywhere in Europe (1.42 ± 0.10 Ma), proving an East-to-West Danubian/Carpathian warm-interglacial dispersal before Western European Atapuerca/Orce.
evidence.limits: Loess soil acidity dissolved hominin fossils; species assignment (presumed H. erectus) rests on chronology and core-flake technology.

evidence.title: Isernia La Pineta (Molise, Southern Italy): ~585 ka Early Homo heidelbergensis Tooth & Butchered Fauna
evidence.dateBasis: Single-crystal 40Ar/39Ar dating (586 ± 2 ka / 583 ± 3 ka) on pyroclastic pumice levels capping the main living surface.
evidence.summary: Dense lakeside elephant, rhinoceros, and steppe-bison butchery pavement yielding Europe's oldest well-dated human deciduous incisor from the MIS 15–14 Middle Pleistocene transition.
evidence.limits: Single isolated infant tooth yields limited craniodental taxonomy.

evidence.title: Ceprano / Campogrande (Latium, Italy): ~450–385 ka Archaic Cranial Vault
evidence.dateBasis: Revised stratigraphic pollen/40Ar/39Ar correlations dating the clay bed of Ceprano calvaria to MIS 11 (~430–385 ka) rather than ~800 ka.
evidence.summary: Complete thick-walled supraorbital braincase lacking clear Neanderthal specializations—now recognized as a key Middle Pleistocene ancestral variant (~400 ka) beside Iberian Sima de los Huesos.
evidence.limits: Highway-bulldozer discovery in 1994 required multi-decade stratigraphic drilling to resolve age.

evidence.title: Barnfield Pit, Swanscombe (Kent, England): ~400 ka Clactonian-to-Acheulean Skull
evidence.dateBasis: Biostratigraphy, amino-acid racemization, and Hoxnian interglacial Thames terrace correlation.
evidence.summary: Three refitting parietal and occipital skull bones of a young woman discovered between 1935 and 1955 showing early incipient Neanderthal occipital traits amid pointed Acheulean handaxes above lower Clactonian flakes.
evidence.limits: Facial skeleton absent; phylogenetic placement debates stem Neanderthal vs. broader H. heidelbergensis.

evidence.title: Bilzingsleben & Steinheim (Germany): ~370–250 ka Interglacial Homo heidelbergensis
evidence.dateBasis: U-series and ESR travertine dating (Bilzingsleben MIS 11/9 travertine; Steinheim MIS 9–7 river gravels).
evidence.summary: Travertine lake-camp preserving massive archaic cranial-and-mandibular fragments (including E7 mandible), small flint/quartz microlithic scrapers, elephant-tusk/bone splinters, and Steinheim's post-distorted proto-Neanderthal skull.
evidence.limits: Travertine claims of circular hut pavements vs. natural spring-channel sorting remain debated.

evidence.title: Vértesszőlős ('Samu') Travertine Spring Site (Hungary): ~350–300 ka Hearths & Occipital
evidence.dateBasis: U-series dates on Danube terrace travertine basins enclosing charred bone concentrations and cranial fragment.
evidence.summary: Rare Central European Middle Pleistocene travertine occupation preserving charred bone-ash hearth lenses, small-pebble Buda industry cores, footprints, and the thick 'Samu' adult occipital bone.
evidence.limits: Single occipital fragment limits full cranial comparison.

evidence.title: Petralona Cave (Chalkidiki, Northern Greece): ~286 ka Encrusted Middle Pleistocene Cranium
evidence.dateLabel: c. 286 thousand years ago (2025 U-series on flowstone crust)
evidence.dateBasis: New 2025 high-precision U-series MC-ICP-MS dating (286 ± 9 ka min age) on calcite coating the famous stalagmite-wedged skull.
evidence.summary: Best-preserved Middle Pleistocene complete human cranium in southeastern Europe, combining heavy archaic supraorbital torus and facial architecture alongside transitional early-Neanderthal/H. heidelbergensis traits.
evidence.limits: 1960 amateur discovery detached primary stratigraphic soil context, now anchored via calcite rind U-series.

evidence.title: Terra Amata & Grotte du Lazaret (Nice, France): ~380–160 ka Mediterranean Shore Camps
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series, and marine beach-terrace sequences spanning Acheulean Terra Amata and early-Neanderthal Lazaret cave.
evidence.summary: Continuous Cote d'Azur beach-to-cave archives capturing seasonal elephant/deer beach butchery, early controlled fire hearths, seaweed bedding traces, and early-Neanderthal parietal/dental fossils.
evidence.limits: Post-depositional beach wave action reworked some Terra Amata artifact vertical spreads.

evidence.title: Pontnewydd Cave (Denbighshire, North Wales): ~225 ka Earliest British Early Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: TL on burned flint, U-series on flowstone, and fauna bracketing volcanic tuff-pebble Levallois tools and taurodont teeth.
evidence.summary: Northernmost MIS 7 European Neanderthal site yielding ~19 taurodont dental & jaw specimens from at least five individuals who shaped volcanic-rock handaxes and Levallois points.
evidence.limits: Debris-flow mudslides washed remains deep inside the karst gallery.

evidence.title: Altamura Man (Lamalunga Cave) & Saccopastore (Italy): ~172–125 ka Neanderthal Skeleton
evidence.dateBasis: Direct U-series on calcite 'popcorn' encrusting Altamura Man (172–130 ka) + ~2015 Saccopastore gravel MIS 5e revision.
evidence.summary: Complete adult early-Neanderthal skeleton fused intact inside limestone cave speleothems—yielding the oldest recovered Neanderthal mtDNA genome alongside Saccopastore's MIS 5e cranial/tooth records near Rome.
evidence.limits: Fragile calcite concretions prevent full physical extraction without damaging cave architecture.

evidence.title: Cova Negra (Xàtiva, Valencia, Spain): ~273–146 ka Paleopathological Neanderthal Child
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, ESR, and micro-CT paleopathology of CN-42170 temporal labyrinth inside Iberian Mousterian levels.
evidence.summary: Multilayered Iberian Neanderthal cave preserving rare inner-ear Down syndrome labyrinth anatomy in an ~6-year-old child who survived well beyond infancy thanks to compassionate collective caregiving.
evidence.limits: Sparse absolute C14 dates in deep strata rely on combined ESR/OSL sediment series.

evidence.title: Gruta da Figueira Brava (Setúbal, Portugal): ~106–86 ka Neanderthal Marine Foraging
evidence.dateBasis: U-series and OSL dating on coastal karst cave chambers rich in charred brown-crab claws, pine nuts, and limpets.
evidence.summary: Conclusive Atlantic coastal evidence proving Last Interglacial Neanderthals systematically harvested roasted brown crabs, mussels, limpets, seals, seabirds, and roasted stone-pine nuts—challenging 'sapiens-only' seafood models.
evidence.limits: Post-glacial sea-level rise flooded lower outer coastal caves across the same Arrábida cliff.

evidence.title: Grotta Guattari & Monte Circeo (Latium, Italy): ~75–50 ka Coastal Hyena Den & Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: ESR, U-series, and landslide-sealing geomorphology yielding 10+ Neanderthal individuals across Pontinian Mousterian.
evidence.summary: Celebrated landslide-sealed coastal cave where the Guattari 1 cranium and 2021 newly excavated Neanderthal remains reveal hyena-den scavenging beside Pontinian flint-pebble coastal industries.
evidence.limits: Early 1939 theories of 'ritual skull cannibalism' were overturned in favor of hyena den accumulation.

evidence.title: Combe-Grenal & Pech de l'Azé I/II/IV (Dordogne, France): ~150–45 ka Reference Mousterian Sequences
evidence.dateBasis: 65+ deep Mousterian layers calibrated via TL on heated flints, ESR/U-series teeth, and manganese-dioxide fire-starting blocks.
evidence.summary: Cornerstone Western European Mousterian master sequences tracing how Périgord Neanderthals shifted from forest deer to cold tundra reindeer hunting while using manganese-dioxide lumps as chemical tinder-lighting catalysts.
evidence.limits: Original 1950s–1960s Bordes excavation zones require ongoing micro-stratigraphic re-dating.

evidence.title: Abric Romaní (Capellades, Catalonia, Spain): ~70–40 ka Preserved Neanderthal Woodwork & Camps
evidence.dateBasis: Continuous U-series/14C calibrated travertine-tufa sequence preserving rare pseudomorph casts of wooden spears, trays & hearths.
evidence.summary: Tufa-sealed shelter preserving spatial hearths, pine-wood pseudomorph tools, a worked bone spear point, sleeping-bed zones, and rapid mobile logistic hunting camps across MIS 4–3.
evidence.limits: Organic wood survived solely as mineral-replaced calcite pseudomorph negatives rather than cellular timber.

evidence.title: Saint-Césaire (La Roche à Pierrot) & La Quina (Charente, France): ~65–40 ka Late Neanderthals
evidence.dateBasis: Hydroxyproline single-amino-acid AMS radiocarbon directly on Saint-Césaire Châtelperronian Neanderthal skeleton.
evidence.summary: Key Charentian Mousterian-to-Châtelperronian transition sites—Saint-Césaire preserves a directly dated ~41 ka late Neanderthal skeleton within Châtelperronian levels alongside Quina's classic stepped-scraper sequence.
evidence.limits: Upper Châtelperronian association mechanics with encroaching Aurignacian groups remain intensely researched.

evidence.title: Grotte du Renne at Arcy-sur-Cure (Yonne, France): ~45–41 ka Châtelperronian Bone Awls & Pendants
evidence.dateBasis: High-precision collagen ultrafiltration AMS dates (Hublin 2012) paired with 2023 identification of modern-human neonate ilium.
evidence.summary: Most celebrated European transition debate site: pierced fox-canine pendants, ring-grooved ivory pins, and bone awls in Level X, yielding both Neanderthal temporal bones/proteomes and a newly recognized H. sapiens neonate hip.
evidence.limits: Contested whether pendants reflect independent Neanderthal symbolism, acculturation, or fine-scale Aurignacian mixing.

evidence.title: Kiik-Koba & Buran-Kaya III (Crimea): ~100–35 ka Neanderthal Burials & Early Crimean Sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: Zooms proteomic identification, 2025 ancient Neanderthal genome from Starosele/Crimea, and 36 ka Buran-Kaya sapiens Gravettian.
evidence.summary: Eastern European steppic peninsula bridge yielding flexed Kiik-Koba Neanderthal foot/child burials, 2025 newly sequenced late-Neanderthal steppe genomes linked to Altai/Caucasus, and early Upper Paleolithic Homo sapiens.
evidence.limits: Cold-stage hiatuses separate late Micoquian Neanderthals and Streletskayan/Aurignacian/Gravettian layers.

evidence.title: Lapa do Picareiro (Estremadura, Portugal): ~41–38 ka Earliest Atlantic Aurignacian Dispersal
evidence.dateBasis: 2020 high-precision AMS bone chronology establishing Early Aurignacian Level GG by ~41.1–38.1 cal ka BP.
evidence.summary: High-precision Iberian sequence documenting rapid westward modern-human expansion to Europe's Atlantic margin right on top of sterile silts above Iberian Mousterian levels—challenging long late-Neanderthal persistence north of the Tagus.
evidence.limits: Diagnostics rely on lithic Dufour/Aurignacian bladelets without Aurignacian human skeletal remains.

evidence.title: Mladeč Caves (Moravia, Czechia): ~35 ka Earliest Direct-Dated Aurignacian Cranial Assemblage
evidence.dateBasis: Direct ultrafiltration AMS dates (~31 ka 14C = ~35.2 cal ka BP) on Mladeč 1, 2, 8, and 9 teeth and bone.
evidence.summary: Largest European Early Upper Paleolithic (Aurignacian) human fossil sample (>5 adults & children alongside split-base bone points), showcasing modern humans living soon after Neanderthal admixture.
evidence.limits: Many specimens were lost during the 1945 Mikulov castle fire, though surviving skulls remain intact.

evidence.title: Kents Cavern & Paviland 'Red Lady' (Britain): ~44–33 ka NW Europe Arrival
evidence.dateBasis: Stratigraphic Bayesian ultrafiltration modeling on Kents Cavern 4 maxilla (~44–41.5 ka) + Paviland burial (~33 ka).
evidence.summary: Northwesternmost threshold of Upper Paleolithic Europe: leaf-point/Lincombian-Ranisian-Jerzmanowician industries, the disputed Kents Cavern KC4 human maxilla, and Paviland Cave's red-ochre ceremonial Gravettian burial in Wales.
evidence.limits: Mixed cave carbonate deposits caused historical debate over KC4's exact stratigraphic depth vs. associated bones.

evidence.title: Riwat & Pabbi Hills (Potwar Plateau, Pakistan): ~1.9–1.2 Ma Earliest South Asian Flakes
evidence.dateBasis: Paleomagnetic Olduvai-subchron gritstone stratigraphy (Riwat T-3 quartzite cobbles & flaked Pabbi Hill channels).
evidence.summary: Deep-channel Siwalik conglomerate embedded quartzite cores and flakes cited as evidence for very early Pliocene–Early Pleistocene hominin dispersal into the northern Indian Subcontinent ahead of South Asian Acheulean.
evidence.limits: Small sample size (handful of undisputed artifacts in conglomerate) sustains debates on natural river percussion.

evidence.title: Yuanmou Basin (Yunnan, SW China): ~1.7 Ma Hominin Incisors & Isochron Dating
evidence.dateBasis: Magnetostratigraphy and 2019 cosmogenic isochron 26Al/10Be burial dating (~1.7 Ma) in Yuanmou Basin Member 4.
evidence.summary: Two shovel-shaped Homo erectus upper central incisors paired with simple quartz/quartzite core-flake artifacts, marking Early Pleistocene colonization of southwestern China's mountain-river basins.
evidence.limits: Two isolated teeth afford restricted cranial anatomy beyond Homo erectus affinity.

evidence.title: Mojokerto (Perning) & Sambungmacan (East/Central Java): ~1.49 Ma–150 ka Javanese Homo erectus
evidence.dateBasis: 2022–2025 Kendeng Hills deltaic tephra 40Ar/39Ar and Madura Strait submerged-shelf Homo erectus studies.
evidence.summary: Mojokerto's Perning juvenile H. erectus braincase (~1.49–1.3 Ma) plus submerged Sunda/Madura Strait fossils reveal Javanese Homo erectus adapted to coastal mangrove-and-riverine Sundaland for over a million years.
evidence.limits: Pleistocene delta reworking makes exact 1.49 Ma vs ~1.0 Ma Perning child bed placement contested.

evidence.title: Wolo Sege (So'a Basin, Flores, Indonesia): 1.02 Ma Open-Sea Wallacean Crossing
evidence.dateBasis: 40Ar/39Ar single-grain plateau dating (1.02 ± 0.02 Ma) on tuff ignimbrite capping stone-tool siltstones.
evidence.summary: Proves hominins crossed deep tectonic straits east of Wallace's Line to settle Flores by one million years ago—ancestral to later small-bodied Mata Menge (~700 ka) and Homo floresiensis (~60 ka).
evidence.limits: Basaltic stone artifacts without associated skeletal fossils in 1.02 Ma level.

evidence.title: Kuldara & Sel'ungur Loess Sites (Tajikistan & Kyrgyzstan): ~900–126 ka Central Asian Corridors
evidence.dateBasis: Deep paleosol-loess Brunhes–Matuyama magnetostratigraphy (Pedocomplexes 12/11 at Kuldara ~900–800 ka) and U-series/fauna at Sel'ungur.
evidence.summary: High-altitude Tian Shan–Pamir loess sequences documenting repeated warm-interglacial hominin movements through inner Central Asia linking West Asian corridors to East/North Asia.
evidence.limits: Low artifact counts per paleosol and disputed tooth taxonomy (presumed archaic/Neanderthal at Sel'ungur).

evidence.title: Bose / Baise Basin (Guangxi, South China): ~803 ka Tektite-Dated Bifacial Large Cutting Tools
evidence.dateBasis: 2024 high-precision 40Ar/39Ar dating on Australasian tektites in primary in-situ association with Acheulean-like cobble handaxes & cleavers.
evidence.summary: Rebuts Movius' rigid 'chopper-vs-handaxe line': Australasian meteorite-tektite impact shower (~803 ka) burned local bamboo forests and locked in situ large bifacial handaxes & cleavers across Guangxi river terraces.
evidence.limits: No skeletal remains within Bose terrace sands; makers inferred to be East Asian Homo erectus.

evidence.title: Nanjing (Tangshan) & Hexian Caves (Lower Yangtze, China): ~620–412 ka Evolved Homo erectus
evidence.dateBasis: TIMS U-series flowstone & combined ESR/U-series tooth enamel dates in Nanjing Huludong and Hexian Longtandong karst caves.
evidence.summary: Partial crania and specialized enamel dental crowns confirming persistence and regional diversification of eastern Chinese Homo erectus into the late Middle Pleistocene.
evidence.limits: Some Huludong 1 vs 2 crania and Hexian dates span wide 200-kyr Middle Pleistocene uncertainty.

evidence.title: Dali & Jinniushan (Shaanxi & Liaoning, China): ~300–260 ka Non-erectus Archaic East Asians
evidence.dateBasis: U-series/ESR combined dates paired with comparative vault morphometrics (~1,120–1,390 cc brain volumes).
evidence.summary: Landmark complete Middle Pleistocene East Asian skulls showing expanded cranial capacities and mosaic non-erectus traits—leading morphological candidates alongside Harbin & Hualongdong for the Denisovan/Homo longi sister clade.
evidence.limits: Lacking direct aDNA or proteomes, assignment to Denisovan vs. related sister clade remains morphological.

evidence.title: Maba (Guangdong) & Xujiayao (Shanxi, China): ~200–130 ka Late Archaic Diversity & Cranial Trauma
evidence.dateBasis: 2025 inner-cranial micro-CT Maba reappraisal + U-series/luminescence dates on Xujiayao lake beds.
evidence.summary: Maba 1 (showing healed depressed frontal blow and mosaic inner-anatomy) plus Xujiayao (~20+ thick-walled skull fragments, giant labyrinthine molars, and congenital parietal anomaly) illuminate late archaic East Asia right before H. sapiens arrivals.
evidence.limits: Wide dating debates around Xujiayao (~200–160 ka vs 100 ka) and lack of molecular DNA.

evidence.title: Calio & Talepu (Walanae Basin, South Sulawesi): Early-to-Middle Pleistocene Sea Crossers
evidence.dateBasis: 2025 Calio Early Pleistocene (>1.0 Ma) dating + 194–118 ka U-series/luminescence chert artifacts beneath Talepu mega-fauna beds.
evidence.summary: Deep-time Wallacean island archaeology proving repeated Early & Middle Pleistocene oceanic crossings to Sulawesi by unknown archaic hominins hundreds of millennia before modern Homo sapiens.
evidence.limits: No hominin body fossils recovered from pre-sapiens Walanae beds.

evidence.title: Penghu 1 Submerged Strait Mandible (Taiwan Channel): Male Denisovan Paleoproteome
evidence.dateBasis: 2025 ancient paleoproteomic confirmation (AMELY/Denisovan-specific amino-acid variants, Science) paired with MIS 6 / MIS 2 sea-level lowstands.
evidence.summary: Robust male mandible dredged from 60–120 m deep Penghu Submarine Channel—proven via 2025 protein sequencing to be a male Denisovan, extending the confirmed Denisovan range into warm subtropical coastal East Asia.
evidence.limits: Dredged marine-shelf context leaves exact MIS 6 (~190–130 ka) vs MIS 4–2 (~70–10 ka) age bracketed by geology.

evidence.title: Nesher Ramla (Central Israel): ~140–120 ka Non-Neanderthal Levantine Archaic Homo
evidence.dateBasis: OSL, TL on burned flints, and U-series dating sealed in an 8 m sinkhole alongside Centripetal Levallois flints.
evidence.summary: Parietal vault and complete mandible with massive archaic third molar—revealing a distinct late surviving Middle Pleistocene Levantine Homo population coexisting and sharing Levallois stone-knapping with early Homo sapiens.
evidence.limits: Debated whether Nesher Ramla fossils represent a new Levantine lineage or an early pre-Neanderthal population.

evidence.title: Dhaba (Son Valley, MP) & Didwana 16R (Rajasthan, India): ~80–48 ka Across Toba Tuff
evidence.dateBasis: Single-grain IRSL/OSL bracketing the Younger Toba Tuff (~74 ka) ash layer in the Middle Son Valley (Clarkson 2020).
evidence.summary: Flagship North Indian terrace documenting Middle Paleolithic Levallois point industries persisting cleanly before, through, and after the ~74 ka Toba super-eruption—consistent with an early H. sapiens or mosaic survival corridor in India.
evidence.limits: No hominin skeletal remains associated directly with Dhaba Levallois levels.

evidence.title: Boker Tachtit (Negev Desert, Israel): ~50–47 ka Initial Upper Paleolithic Benchmark
evidence.dateBasis: High-resolution radiocarbon and OSL calibration tracing Levels 1–4 refitting reduction cores from Levallois to prismatic blades.
evidence.summary: World-famous step-by-step technological workshop where conjoined flint nodules prove an in-situ technological transformation from Middle Paleolithic Levallois points into full Upper Paleolithic Emireh/blade cores ~50 ka.
evidence.limits: No human fossils recovered from Boker Tachtit floors.

evidence.title: Ksar Akil ('Egbert' & 'Ethelruda', Lebanon): ~45–40 ka Early Levantine Homo sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian shell-carbonate & enamel radiocarbon models bracketing Level XXV maxilla 'Ethelruda' (~45.9 ka) and XVII skeleton 'Egbert'.
evidence.summary: 23-meter Levantine rockshelter anchor containing pierced Tritia shell beads, Initial Upper Paleolithic blades, and two Homo sapiens juveniles charting our species' overland expansion out of the Levant toward Europe.
evidence.limits: 1930s excavation records and marine-reservoir offsets on dated shell beads created minor model divergence (~46 vs ~43 ka).

evidence.title: Üçağızlı & Karaïn Caves (Southern Anatolia, Turkey): ~250–41 ka Neanderthal-to-Sapiens Margin
evidence.dateBasis: U-series/ESR dates on deeper Karaïn Neanderthal beds plus AMS/shell-bead horizons at Initial UP Üçağızlı (~43–41 ka).
evidence.summary: Key Anatolian corridor pairing Karaïn's deep Taurus karst Neanderthal occupations and teeth with Üçağızlı's rich ~41 ka Initial Upper Paleolithic marine-shell beads and early Homo sapiens teeth.
evidence.limits: Shattered limestone rubble in upper coastal shelters mixes thin hearth lenses.

evidence.title: Okladnikov & Kara-Bom Caves (Altai Mountains, Siberia): ~47–40 ka Easternmost Neanderthals & Early UP
evidence.dateBasis: aDNA verification of easternmost Neanderthal genomes (~44–38 ka Okladnikov) + Initial UP blade sequence (Kara-Bom ~47–43 ka).
evidence.summary: Deep Siberian caves yielding nuclear/mtDNA confirming Neanderthals ranged as far east as the Altai (~2,000 km further east than Europe), matched closely at Kara-Bom by North Eurasia's earliest ~47 ka Initial Upper Paleolithic blade industry.
evidence.limits: Complex slope cryo-turbation originally skewed bulk bone collagen dates older prior to amino-acid AMS revision.

evidence.title: Tolbor-16 & Salkhit Skullcap (Northern Mongolia): ~45–34 ka Early Steppe Homo sapiens
evidence.dateBasis: 2019 Tolbor-16 OSL/14C blade chronology (Zwyns ~45 ka) paired with ~34.9 ka Salkhit calvaria ancient genome.
evidence.summary: Definitive northern steppe route into Northeast Asia—Tolbor-16's 45,000-year-old systematic Upper Paleolithic blades and Salkhit's sequenced sapiens genome carrying ~1.7% Denisovan admixture alongside Ancestral North Eurasian links.
evidence.limits: Subaerial paleosol erosion thinned initial blade layers outside frozen alluvial pockets.

evidence.title: Shuidonggou Locality 1–2 (Ningxia, NW China): ~41–34 ka Ordos Steppic Blade & Bead Oasis
evidence.dateBasis: OSL and AMS radiocarbon across hearth-rich yellow loess terrace sequences above the Yellow River tributary.
evidence.summary: Showcase East Asian Initial Upper Paleolithic settlement demonstrating southward blade-core diffusion from Mongolia alongside China's earliest ostrich-eggshell disc beads, bone needles, and organized camp hearths.
evidence.limits: Upper terrace deposits lacked preserved human skeletal bones.

evidence.title: Tabon Cave Pleistocene Occupation & Tibia (Palawan, Philippines): ~47–30 ka Wallacean Foragers
evidence.dateBasis: U-series direct dates on Tabon human tibia (~47 ± 11 ka), cap (~16.5 ka), and 2023 micro-wear basket/fiber evidence (39–33 ka).
evidence.summary: Deep coastal karst limestone chamber overlooking South China Sea beds—yielding earliest securely U-series dated Homo sapiens fossils in the Philippines alongside ~39–33 ka stone tools bearing stripped plant-fiber basketry wear.
evidence.limits: Disturbed 1960s test pits leave frontal cap (~16.5 ka) vs tibia (~47 ka) associations non-synchronous.

evidence.title: Leang Bulu Bettue (Maros Karst, South Sulawesi): ~40–30 ka Portable Engraved Rock & Pendants
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & U-series dates on sealed karst cave layers containing pierced babirusa/bear-cuscus phalanx pendants and incised anoa plaques.
evidence.summary: Critical stratigraphic occupation matching Sulawesi's famous wall art: yielding portable geometric/figurative engraved stones, perforated endemic mammal pendants, red ochre crayons, and flaking sequences dated 40–30 ka.
evidence.limits: Lower 200–100 ka gravel layers below 40 ka yielded sparse pre-sapiens cores without hominins.

evidence.title: Boodie Cave (Barrow Island, NW Australia): ~50–46 ka Pleistocene Shelf Marine Foraging & Beads
evidence.dateBasis: Single-grain OSL and AMS radiocarbon by Veth et al. (2017) & Hook et al. (2024) on transported Melo baler shell & scaphopod beads.
evidence.summary: Benchmark northwest Sahul shelter proving coastal maritime economies arrived by ~50 ka: people carried marine Melo shells and perforated scaphopod beads >20 km inland over exposed Pleistocene plains prior to island cutoff.
evidence.limits: Pre-40 ka layers contain low artifact counts per cubic meter compared to post-glacial shellfish middens.

evidence.title: Carpenter's Gap 1, Riwi Cave & Juukan 2 (Kimberley & Pilbara, WA): ~47–45 ka Deep Aboriginal Innovation
evidence.dateBasis: Bayesian 14C/OSL chronologies (Maloney 2018; Balme 2018; Slack 2024) recovering ~49–44 ka ground-edge axe flake & botanical caches.
evidence.summary: Premier northwest Australian shelters preserving an early ground-edge axe fragment (~49–44 ka at Carpenter's Gap 1), ~46 ka ochre-stained wall fragments, desert botanical seeds (Riwi ~45 ka), and Puutu Kunti Kurrama and Pinikura deep Pilbara ancestry (Juukan 2 ~47 ka).
evidence.limits: Deep karst sands preserve fine plant/charcoal organics better than bone collagen in tropical heat.

evidence.title: Devil's Lair (Margaret River, SW Australia): ~48–45 ka Karst Bone Point & Bead Shelter
evidence.dateBasis: ABO-stepped charcoal AMS, ESR on macropod teeth, and OSL quartz dates (~48–45 ka) in cave flowstone strata.
evidence.summary: Southwesternmost Australian Pleistocene cave sequence showing rapid Sahul coastal dispersal down to 34°S within millennia—preserving a kangaroo fibula bead, pointed bone tools, and engraved calcrete plaques.
evidence.limits: Upper/mid-1970s radiocarbon ages required redating to pierce the ~40 ka barrier.

evidence.title: Puritjarra Rockshelter (Cleland Hills, Central Australia): ~35 ka Red-Centre Desert Adaptation
evidence.dateBasis: OSL & AMS dates on red-ochre quarry smears carried >125 km from Karrku across arid central Australia.
evidence.summary: Earliest securely dated human occupation of the hyper-arid Red Centre of Australia—documenting thin mobile desert bands hauling prized Karrku red ochre and fine chert into Central Australia's MacDonnell margins by 35 ka.
evidence.limits: Extremely slow desert sand accumulation produced compressed basal artifact horizons.

evidence.title: Bobongara (Huon Peninsula, Papua New Guinea): ~40 ka Uplifted Reef Terrace Axes
evidence.dateBasis: TL/ESR and U-series dating of volcanic ashes draping uplifted Pleistocene coral terraces on the Vitiaz Strait.
evidence.summary: Landmark Near Oceanic Sahul settlement along the mountainous Huon Peninsula coast preserving heavy waisted volcanic-stone axes used to thin highland/coastal rainforest canopies by ~40 ka.
evidence.limits: Uplifted limestone terraces yield weathered basalt/andesite stone axes without human bone preservation.

evidence.title: Kilu Cave (Buka Island, Northern Solomon Islands): ~32 ka Deep-Ocean Crossing & Taro Starch
evidence.dateBasis: Marine-shell & charcoal radiocarbon (~28.7 ka 14C = ~32.5 cal ka BP) paired with microscopic Colocasia taro starch grains on stone tools.
evidence.summary: Earth's furthest open-ocean Pleistocene human outpost: seafarers crossed >140 km of open blue water out of New Ireland to colonize Buka Island by 32 ka, exploiting reef shark/tuna and processing wild Alocasia/Colocasia taro corms.
evidence.limits: Small test excavation yielded no human skeletal fossils prior to later Lapita horizons.

evidence.title: Warreen & Parmerpar Meethaner Caves (Lutruwita / Tasmania): ~35 ka Ice-Age Southernmost Humans
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon across Bassian land-bridge colonization horizons (~35 cal ka BP) with transported Darwin Crater impactite glass.
evidence.summary: Southernmost known Ice Age humans on Earth (~42.5°S): Palawa ancestors crossed the ephemeral Bassian Plain during low sea levels, hunting red-necked wallabies in glacial valleys and carrying green meteorite glass >100 km.
evidence.limits: Bass Strait flooding after ~12–10 ka isolated Tasmanian communities cleanly from mainland Australia.
